text:
maria_g: Customer reported a 413 when calling /v1/rerank. Payload is ~120 docs + a long query. Error body is unhelpful: "Request too large". Can we triage and suggest a clear workaround and better error wording?

alex.m: Can you paste the exact request and the response body they got? Also the request_id if it's in logs.

maria_g: Pasting redacted repro (customer gave permission):
```
POST /v1/rerank
Content-Type: application/json
{
  "model": "rwdn/rerank-v1",
  "query": "How do I reset my billing account and migrate invoices? (long query with context) ...",
  "documents": [
    {"id": "doc_1", "text": "<~8k chars of policy>"},
    {"id": "doc_2", "text": "<~6k chars>"},
    ... (total 120 docs) ...
  ]
}
```
Response: HTTP/1.1 413 \n```
{"error":"Request too large","code":413,"message":"total tokens 95321 > request token limit 65536"}
```
They said message doesn't tell them which part to trim (query vs per-doc vs doc count).

support-bot: Automated note: request_id=rt-0a12bf, trace=trace-9f3.

samuel: Triage checklist: 1) confirm tokenization used (we count tokens with RW-tokenizer), 2) ask customer to run our helper to compute token totals, 3) recommend chunking docs into batches (e.g., 10-20) or prefilter with embeddings before rerank.

alex.m: Is the platform enforcing both per-document and per-request token caps? If so, error should say which cap was hit.

maria_g: Yes — current enforcement: per-doc token cap = 8192, per-request aggregate cap = 65536. In this case aggregate cap was exceeded (95321 > 65536). Also note a single doc could hit per-doc cap and return same 413 with a different message today, which confuses users.

eng-runtime: Thanks for the repro and request_id. We can reproduce locally with the supplied payload. Two asks: 1) please collect the incoming bytes and kernel logs for rt-0a12bf, 2) we should change the error body to include fields: {"limit_type":"request_tokens","limit_value":65536,"actual":95321} so users know exactly what to change. Happy to ship a small patch to make error bodies explicit.

maria_g: I'll ask the customer for logs and give a workaround. Proposed support reply: 1) explain limit semantics (per-doc vs per-request), 2) provide quick chunking script, 3) suggest prefiltering with embeddings + top-K then rerank. Anyone want to review the wording?

alex.m: +1. Add a one-line suggested sentence: "If you need to rank many long docs, run embeddings to filter down to ~20 candidates per query, then rerank those". Also include a curl example for batch rerank: 
```
# pseudo: split docs into chunks of N and hit /v1/rerank for each chunk; merge scores client-side
for chunk in chunks(docs, 15):
  curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank -d '{"query":"...","documents": chunk }'
```

samuel: I'll file a docs/ux ticket to add explicit examples and the token-calculator snippet. Filing: https://redwood.internal/issue/RWD-1274 (internal link). Please note: make sure we don't recommend naive concatenation of large docs — recommend snippeting relevant sections first.

eng-runtime: For the patch, we'll: 1) update runtime to return structured limit info, 2) ensure status remains 413 for payload size but body is explicit, 3) add telemetry to surface top offending field (per_doc vs aggregate). ETA for small patch: 2 business days, then a docs PR to follow.

maria_g: I'll send the customer the workaround and ask if they want us to handle chunking server-side (offer to help with a short script). Also asking PM to prioritize the clearer error message.

alex.m: Draft support snippet to send to customer (feel free to copy): 
```
Short-term workaround:
1) If you can, reduce the number of docs per call to <= 15 and rerank in batches.
2) If docs are very long, pre-extract relevant passages (snippeting) before reranking.
3) Use embeddings to prefilter: encode docs, compute similarity to query, take top ~50 then rerank in chunks of 15.

Example chunking pseudocode: (python)
chunks = [docs[i:i+15] for i in range(0, len(docs), 15)]
results = []
for c in chunks:
    r = client.rerank(model='rwdn/rerank-v1', query=query, documents=c)
    results.extend(r.scores)
# merge scores and sort
```

samuel: Also requested: a short FAQ blurb about "413 vs 400" and why we return 413 when request body/token budget is exceeded. We'll pair that with the clearer JSON fields.

maria_g: Thanks all — I'll update thread once customer confirms and when eng-runtime ships the patch. Closing for now. :white_check_mark:

eng-runtime: noted. Will post PR link when ready. :pkg:
